title: Fractions: compare equal parts / Fracciones: comparar partes iguales

lessons.title: 1. Equal parts / Partes iguales
lessons.objective: Explain what the numerator and denominator count.
lessons.prerequisite_check: Can you split a rectangle into four equal areas?
lessons.content: A fraction describes equal parts of one whole. In 3/8, the denominator 8 counts all equal parts and the numerator 3 counts the selected parts. / Una fracción describe partes iguales de una unidad. En 3/8, el denominador 8 indica todas las partes iguales y el numerador 3 las partes elegidas.
lessons.worked_example: Shade 3 of 8 equal strips: the shaded fraction is 3/8.
lessons.feedback: Check that all five parts have equal area and exactly two are selected.
lessons.delayed_review: Tomorrow, explain 4/7 without looking at the lesson.

lessons.title: 2. Compare common denominators / Comparar denominadores iguales
lessons.objective: Compare fractions of the same whole with a common denominator.
lessons.content: For fractions of the same whole with equal denominators, each part has the same size. More selected parts means a larger fraction. Thus 5/8 is larger than 3/8. / En fracciones de la misma unidad y con denominadores iguales, cada parte tiene el mismo tamaño. Más partes elegidas dan una fracción mayor: 5/8 es mayor que 3/8.
lessons.worked_example: 7/10 > 4/10 because seven equal tenths exceed four equal tenths.
lessons.independent_attempt: Which is larger, 2/9 or 6/9? Explain without using decimals.
lessons.feedback: Compare numerators only after checking that the whole and denominator match.
lessons.delayed_review: After two days, compare 3/11 and 8/11 and give a reason.

lessons.title: 3. Independent retrieval / Recuperación independiente
lessons.objective: Choose and justify a comparison, including the limits of the rule.
lessons.prerequisite_check: State the conditions for comparing numerators directly.
lessons.content: Try before asking for a hint. Compare 4/7 and 6/7. Then explain why the same rule alone cannot compare 3/5 and 4/9. / Intenta resolverlo antes de pedir una pista. Compara 4/7 y 6/7. Después explica por qué esta regla por sí sola no permite comparar 3/5 y 4/9.
lessons.worked_example: 1/6 < 5/6: same whole, same denominator, fewer selected sixths.
lessons.independent_attempt: Write one valid comparison and one pair where this rule does not apply.
lessons.feedback: A sound explanation names equal parts of the same whole; a larger denominator alone does not imply a larger fraction.
lessons.delayed_review: One week later, solve a new common-denominator comparison without hints.
